query: Prior calculations on concentrated alloys examined variations in atomic mass and force constants, temperature-dependent lattice heat transport, or DFT-derived elastic properties coupled to analytical conductivity estimates; some estimates require a Debye temperature. The cited simulations generally represented perfect, defect-free bulk crystals. Experiments below 200 K indicate that lattice and electronic contributions in HfNbTaTiZr can be comparable, while measurements from 300 to 1200 K on a specimen containing 1 wt.% oxygen report total conductivity of 10–17 W/(K m). Available analytical approaches do not capture all relevant atomic-scale complexity in refractory high-entropy alloys, and separate transport studies do not establish a predictive solution for this alloy. Given these constraints, what testable hypothesis could an unspecified new predictive approach make for HfNbTaTiZr without conflating lattice and electronic heat transport? Explain why it should outperform earlier approaches, quantify the expected improvement, define its temperature and sample applicability limits, identify supporting observations from the cited work, and specify decisive comparisons with low- and high-temperature measurements that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: In equiatomic, defect-free polycrystalline HfNbTaTiZr (≤0.1 wt% O), a unified predictive model combining DFT-calculated phonon dispersions with mass‐disorder scattering and ab initio Boltzmann electron transport will predict the lattice thermal conductivity (κ_L) to within ±10% and the electronic thermal conductivity (κ_e) within ±15% over 100–1200 K, reducing total conductivity error by ~20% compared to existing Debye‐based analytical methods.
generation.material_initial_state: Defect-free, polycrystalline equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr with ≤0.1 wt% oxygen, average grain size ~10 µm, no extended defects.
generation.intervention: Application of a unified DFT-based phonon dispersion calculation with explicit mass‐ and force-constant disorder scattering plus ab initio Boltzmann transport for electrons.
generation.conditions: 100–1200 K in inert atmosphere on polycrystalline samples with ≤0.1 wt% O.
generation.structural_mediator: Atomic mass and force-constant disorder arising from size and mass mismatch among Hf, Nb, Ta, Ti, Zr.
generation.mechanism: Mass- and force-constant disorder cause enhanced phonon scattering captured by DFT‐computed phonon linewidths; alloy disorder electron scattering is treated via ab initio Boltzmann transport.
generation.predicted_outcome: κ_L predicted within ±10% of experiment, κ_e within ±15%, total κ within ±12% across 100–1200 K. Example: κ_total(300 K)=12 ± 1.5 W/(m·K) vs. previously reported 10–17 W/(m·K).
generation.baseline: Analytical Debye-temperature models coupled to DFT elastic constants yield ≈30% error in κ predictions for HfNbTaTiZr.
generation.boundary: Valid for equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr, defect-free polycrystals, O content ≤1 wt%, temperature 100–1200 K, average grain size ≳1 µm, negligible dislocation density.
generation.uncertainty: ±3% near 300 K (mass-disorder parameter uncertainty), up to ±10% near 1200 K (neglected higher-order anharmonicity).

falsification_experiment.design: (1) Low-temperature (10–200 K) 3ω measurements under magnetic field to separate κ_L and κ_e; (2) High-temperature (300–800 K) steady-state thermal conductivity and Hall-effect electrical resistivity to deconvolute κ_e and κ_L.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: Hypothesis is falsified if predicted κ_L or κ_e deviates by more than 15% from measured values in either the low-T or high-T regimes.
